name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-20E 'Thunderclap'
description:
Kang-Petrov's first electromagnetic accelerator rifle brings railgun technology to the mass market. The KPA-20E Thunderclap uses a single-stage magnetic acceleration system to fire 3mm steel-core projectiles at supersonic velocity. It lacks the power and range of Arcturus' MAR-8X, but at Φ5,500 it costs less than a quarter of the military platform and requires no BCI integration to operate.

The Thunderclap's capacitor system is integrated into the rifle's stock, providing 40 shots per charge. Recharging takes 120 seconds from a standard power outlet. The weapon has no moving bolt or gas system — projectiles are loaded from a gravity-fed hopper atop the receiver and accelerated through the barrel by electromagnetic coils. This mechanical simplicity means there are no extraction or feeding failures, though the hopper is vulnerable to contamination if left uncovered.

Critics from the premium arms manufacturers dismiss the Thunderclap as a toy — its 3mm projectiles lack the penetration of larger tungsten penetrators, and the single-stage acceleration limits velocity. But for operators who want electromagnetic capability without corporate entanglement, the KPA-20E democratizes access to technology that was previously exclusive to military budgets.
specifications:
caliber: 3mm steel-core projectile
effective_range: 400m
rate_of_fire: 200 rpm (capacitor-limited)
magazine_capacity: 40 projectiles per charge
weight: 3.8 kg
tactical_use: The KPA-20E provides electromagnetic capability at a fraction of military cost. While it cannot match the MAR-8X's penetration or range, the Thunderclap's steel-core projectiles defeat Level II body armor and most personal barriers. The lack of chemical propellant means no muzzle flash and minimal sound signature — the electromagnetic hum and supersonic crack are the only signatures. Useful for operators who need the advantages of EM acceleration without the expense.
cultural_context: The Thunderclap represents Kang-Petrov's mission to democratize weapons technology. Corporate arms manufacturers have lobbied for restrictions on civilian electromagnetic weapons, arguing that the technology is inherently military-grade. Kang-Petrov's legal team has fought every restriction, positioning the KPA-20E as a test case for whether corponations can monopolize entire categories of arms technology.
story_hooks: Arcturus Defense Solutions is funding a legal campaign to classify all electromagnetic weapons as military-exclusive technology — if they succeed, every KPA-20E owner becomes a felon overnight.
A hacker collective has published modifications that double the Thunderclap's acceleration power. The mod works, but the capacitor stock has a 5% chance of catastrophic failure per shot.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular assault rifle with a distinctly futuristic profile. The body appears almost skeletal compared to conventional firearms—stripped of gas tubes and bolt carriers, replaced by visible electromagnetic coil arrays along the barrel. The receiver has clean, minimal geometry with an industrial aesthetic. The most distinctive feature is the gravity-fed hopper mounted atop the receiver like an inverted funnel, creating an asymmetrical silhouette. Overall impression: lean, efficient, more engineering than ornamentation.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 96 cm | Barrel length: 55 cm | Receiver width: 8 cm | Hopper height: 12 cm above receiver
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced but substantial at 3.8 kg—the integrated capacitor stock provides weight distribution that keeps the weapon stable in the shoulders. Not lightweight, but the weight is purposeful rather than unwieldy. Feels precisely engineered rather than heavy.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum alloy receiver with steel barrel and electromagnetic coil assembly. Polymer composite panels for thermal management over the capacitor housing.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed aluminum receiver. The barrel shows visible electromagnetic coil windings in anodized dark bronze. Heat-dissipation panels on the stock feature a subtle crosshatch texture to aid grip.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray and brushed aluminum | Accents: dark bronze electromagnetic coil windings, thin accent lines in electric blue along the capacitor cooling vents
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated cooling ridges—slightly warm to the touch when charged. The stock features rubberized panels that transition to bare aluminum heat-sink fins at the rear.
distinctive_features: Gravity-fed hopper mounted atop receiver with transparent polycarbonate sides showing 3mm steel-core projectiles
Visible electromagnetic coil arrays along entire barrel length with bronze-anodized finish
Capacitor housing in the stock with thin electric-blue status indicator lines
Thermal vents along receiver sides with crosshatch pattern
No visible trigger guard—minimalist firing mechanism
Three-point balance rail system on bottom of receiver
Small red LED charge indicator on the right side of the stock
Kang-Petrov maker's mark stamped on the left receiver flat
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Kang-Petrov Arms logo stamped on left receiver flat | 'KPA-20E THUNDERCLAP' engraved on barrel shroud | Serial number plate mounted on right side of stock | Small certification mark indicating Tier 2+ licensing approval
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory finish on new units; field-worn examples show minor aluminum scuffing on grip areas and dust accumulation in thermal vent crosshatching. The hopper accumulates projectile residue and atmospheric dust if uncovered during operation. Well-maintained examples retain the bright electric-blue capacitor indicator lines; neglected units show dulled or flickering LEDs.
